lines: In a small pottery shop in old Kyoto, Takeo made a hundred bowls a week.
But one bowl in the house was never for sale.
It had belonged to his wife.
Every evening he drank his tea from it, slowly... the way she used to.
One afternoon, his granddaughter Hana reached up to hold it.
She hid the pieces under her sleeve, and cried until she could not breathe.
That night, Takeo found them. He did not say a word.
He took the pieces down to his bench... and worked by lamplight until morning.
At dawn, the bowl was back in its place. Whole again, with seams of shining gold.

lines.say: When something we love breaks, we do not throw it away.
We fill the cracks with gold.

lines: Because the places where we broke... can become the most beautiful part of us.
